thinking: Thinking: Candidate 2 evaluates the CPD report on Australian voter dissatisfaction with major political parties and the desire for greater policy influence. Stated claims highlight a healthy belief in democratic ideals coupled with profound frustration over major party self-interest and lobbying. Ground reality confirms long-term survey data (Essential Research/CPD pulse) showing declining trust in traditional politics and a rise in minor parties/independents. Stated forces lean toward Good Preference; actual forces reflect a moderate alignment with systemic awakening (LG/GG) as citizens push back against establishment capture. subject: Voters want greater say over national policy as dismay with major parties grows
posts:
Two-thirds of Australians demand greater say in policy as trust in major parties hits a decade low.
Evidence: CPD report, Essential Research, 65% survey consensus
#Aletheia #AusPol

The CPD report frames rising voter frustration as a democratic wake-up call urging major parties to listen and share policy priorities.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Decade-long polling data confirms severe disconnect between voters and self-interested political elites, driving a steady shift toward minor parties.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.7, +0.6) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Awakening.
Decade-long polling exposes systemic disconnect from major parties, fueling a healthy democratic demand for grassroots policy control.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.3, z: 1)

- Centre for Policy Development: PASS (0.8, 0.7) — Rigorous long-term polling.
- Australian Electorate: PASS (0.7, 0.5) — Constructive push for reform.
A new Centre for Policy Development report reveals 65% of Australians want greater influence over public policy as trust in major parties wanes.

The Bright Side:
Growing voter engagement with minor parties and independents signals a robust democratic demand for decentralised policy control.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing institutional fatigue with democratic collapse on the Lyrical plane; voters want reform, not the end of democracy.

Social Physics Analysis:
Australian voters are executing a smart altruistic loop, demanding transparent policy inclusion and pushing back against elite self-interest through democratic channels.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map systemic public frustration to institutional realities, it plots a direct trajectory toward Awakening through democratic realignment.

The Unavoidable Truth: Citizens consistently demand genuine participation over elite-driven policy making.

The Unavoidable Lie: Major political parties naturally reform without external electoral pressure.

Alethekanon:
Empirical polling lays bare the widening chasm between institutional elites and a politically fatigued citizenry. Democratic renewal requires structural listening.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to watch everyday people feel ignored by the very leaders they elected, yet inspiring that they still care deeply about a fair democracy.

Brothekanon:
Aussies are completely sick of the major parties ignoring what matters, and this new CPD report proves everyone wants a real say in how the country is run.

Spirithekanon:
"Where there is no guidance, a people falls, but in an abundance of counselors there is safety." Proverbs 11:14 PASS
True political health requires listening to the wider community rather than hoarding power in narrow corridors.
